resolved_conflicts.explanation: Nomination gives C.S. Erickson on cover and C.J. Erickson in narrative; LighthouseFriends gives Charles J. Erickson of Seattle.
Nomination says the 1898 frame fog-signal building burned in 1916; Commissioner's estimates for 1916 to 1921 still describe the steam plant in an old frame building. Unresolved.
Light-House Board: 26 Nov 1898 received, installed 16 Feb 1899; LighthouseFriends: received 15 Feb 1899.

notes_for_editor: Corpus has no Lighthouse Board reports for FY1898, 1902-1915 and newspaper searches found nothing, so the wreck/rescue chapter is thin; the Bulletin 1912-17 index lists a rescue at Grays Harbor (assistant Henry T. Williams, Bulletin p.56) that was not located in the text. Disagreements stated in text: tower height (92/110 ft nomination vs 107 LF; record 33 m), builder initials, Zauner's earlier station, Settles name/dates, Jacobsen end year (1939 vs 1945), electrification (1931/1933), appropriation sums, land payment year (Dec 1896 per LHB vs 1895 per LF), fog building 1926 vs 1927. Light range in record (18 nm) not verified; nomination says 27 miles, LF 16 miles for the original lens. LF is copyrighted: facts paraphrased only. Pages for Light-House Board reports 1900 and 1901 cited by scan page; 1897 p.183 from index. Fact-check 2026-10-22: roster expanded to the full USLHS list (Scannell and Vanderpool from LighthouseFriends since the archive page prints Scannell's dates garbled); fog-signal burn date 1916 conflicts with reports to 1921; 1931-32 storm item is from OCR'd Bulletin 1932 PDF p.15 (dates read from garbled OCR, story says only mid-December to early January). Nomination's 1977 sheet and 2008-09 form are both cited as [1]; the tours sentence is dated to 2008-09.
